  \par\vspace{3pt}
  \begin{minipage}{\textwidth}\fontsize{7}{8.4}\selectfont
  \textit{Timing boundaries.} I/O+ is a measured serialized host-to-host call, including input/output transfers and invocation, with setup excluded. A100/Groq use PCIe; Graphcore uses the deployed IPU fabric. A100 Resident is CUDA-event elapsed time for a captured graph with device-resident tensors (including HBM access); Active is the union of profiled kernel/device-memory intervals with idle gaps excluded. Groq Schedule is the successful executable\textquotesingle s compiler cycle estimate. IPU Active reconstructs compute, internal exchange and internal synchronization phases.
  \par\smallskip
  \textit{CS-3 estimates.} Stream is the predicted steady-state interval with modeled streaming stalls; First is the predicted first compiled iteration. Neither is a measured host-to-host call. Native sums the compiler\textquotesingle s wafer-native operation cycles assuming preloaded data/layouts, resident code and serial operations; Native+ctx also retains the original context-switch cycle budget. Both D columns are conditional component budgets, not predictions from a newly compiled resident executable or proof of memory-placement feasibility.
  \par\smallskip
  \textsuperscript{a} IIR profiling perturbs timing; its active estimate exceeds the same process\textquotesingle s capture-disabled resident interval and is diagnostic only. \textsuperscript{b} CS-3 has uncosted host helpers (MVT addition; GESUMMV/GEMM reduction/distribution), so the D columns omit required remapping costs. Independent runs and instrumentation can also make active estimates exceed archived elapsed medians; differences are not isolated transfer costs. -- denotes unavailable qualified timing evidence, not zero latency. Case IDs and source hashes are recorded in the accompanying CSV.
  \end{minipage}}
